 SALT LAKE CITY (KUTV) — Two recalls announced October 22 involve products that could cause serious injuries or death.
 A Chinese online seller is recalling about 94 CIYTI light-up princess costumes because children can easily access button-cell batteries inside the included crown, wand and remote control.
 Swallowed button batteries can cause internal chemical burns, serious injuries or death. No incidents or injuries have been reported.
 The costumes were sold on Amazon from February through June 2025 for between $21 and $35.
 Consumers should take the costumes away from children immediately and contact the seller for a full refund. Customers must write “RECALLED” on the dress, crown, wand and remote control, dispose of the products and submit a photograph. Batteries should be handled according to local hazardous-waste procedures.

 VQQQ is recalling about 100 natural-gas patio heaters because components can malfunction and release gas, creating fire and burn hazards that could cause serious injuries or death.
 The recall covers models VQQQ-A1 and VQQQ-001. The heaters were sold on Amazon from July 2024 through August 2026 for about $346. No incidents or injuries have been reported.
 Consumers should stop using the heaters immediately, close the valve at the portable gas source and disconnect the gas hose. VQQQ is offering a full refund. Customers must mark the heater’s base “Recalled,” submit a photograph and dispose of the product.
